text.p: Following are highlights of the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Hunt of war criminals in Bosnia-Herzegovina begins. SFOR has arrested two people, one of whom Mirko Kovacevic was in the Bosnian Serb leadership.
- Two people die in clashes between police and Albanian demonstrators in Gostivar, Macedonia.
- Bosnian Croats and Moslems sign an agreement on the joint police forces in Mostar area.
- The National Bank of Croatia says the IMF's decision to delay the second tranche of its loan will have no serious economic repercussions.
- Grammar school students will soon be able to choose the subjects they want to be taught, Education Minister Ljilja Vokic says in an interview.
- There are no more banks needing rehabilitation at the moment, says central bank governor Marko Skreb.
- Croatia and Indonesia soon expected to sign agreements to avoid double taxation and promote mutual investments.
- The river port in Vukovar is being rebuilt with the help of $6.6 million donated by the Belgian government.
- Skolska Knjiga publisher, which is almost entirely owned by small shareholders, becomes a takeover target of three different buyers.
- IMF stops the second, 28.8-million special drawing rights or $40-million tranche of the three-year loan to Croatia.
- Viktor Lenac repair docks lists 1.06 million shares on the Zagreb Stock Exchange.
- It is still uncertain whether the NATO-led action aimed at apprehending indictees of The Hague war crimes tribunal in Bosnia will involve Radovan Karadzic.
- Croatia begins implementing a law regulating the management of buildings and office blocks from contributions by the owners of flats and business premises.

- Theologian Adalbert Rebic comments on the papal decision on a new Zagreb Archbishop: There was some disagreement about a candidate from the Zagreb diocese so the Holy See chose another candidate, unburdened by squabbles and ambitions of a certain environment. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
